claims.text: The driver's marked arrival at 08:06:50 is a self-reported button press and is not corroborated by his own device trace. Under the arrival test in the no-show policy the driver's arrival event must be corroborated within the arrival radius that POL-NS-21 sets at 50 m for a STANDARD pickup zone, and arrival_check reports corroborated = false: the nearest fix inside the 120 s window around the arrival event is index 18 at 08:04:50, 476.59 m from the Block 251 pickup, and that fix reports an accuracy of 8.0 m, inside the 25 m GPS accuracy filter, so the reading is not an artefact of a bad fix. At no point in the window did the vehicle come closer than 476.59 m, and from 08:06:50 to 08:18:50 every fix is stationary at roughly 650 m from the pickup. The driver was never at the pickup point, so the premise of a rider no-show - a driver waiting at the pickup the rider failed to reach - is absent from the record.

Because the driver never reached the pickup, he failed to arrive at the pickup location by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes: scheduled_at is 08:10:00 and POL-NS-24 allows 300 s (08:15:00), and the trace shows him stationary hundreds of metres away through that deadline and past the cancellation at 08:19:10. POL-NS-24 therefore applies and any fee charged is refunded in full, so the 5.00 SGD charged at 08:19:14 must be returned to the rider. The second limb of POL-NS-24 - the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit - is not claimed: the record shows the driver did send a chat message and place one in-app call, so the contact attempt existed even though the arrival did not.

POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee only when the driver cancels after the free wait - that is, after waiting at the pickup for a rider who has not come. Here the driver's own chat message at 08:07:10 reads 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark', while the trip record's pickup label and the rider's contemporaneous 08:11:30 message place the meeting point at Block 251, so on the parties' own statements the driver waited at a different block and the trip failed at the driver's end, not the rider's. The driver's later message at 08:14:00, 'I'm at the pickup point waiting already', is a bare assertion contradicted by his own device trace at that timestamp, whereas the rider's account matches the booking record's own pickup label. The fee condition in POL-NS-22 is not satisfied and the fee cannot be pinned on a rider no-show.

I do not press POL-NS-23: the driver's contact obligation is met on this record. The chat log carries a driver message at 08:07:10 and the trip record carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 08:15:20, both before cancelled_at at 08:19:10, so obligation_met is true and that ground is conceded. The rider's case rests on the arrival and location failures, which POL-NS-23 does not touch.

No traffic advisory was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05057-01 is a MISSING artifact, carries no payload, and its admissibility weight is 0.0 with the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it is cited here as an absence and cannot carry any fact. Its absence is still worth naming, because it forecloses the only external explanation available on the face of the record: nothing in this file suggests that road or traffic conditions, rather than the driver's own choice of stopping point, kept the vehicle 476.59 m from the pickup for the whole waiting window.

The money on the ledger is undisputed: the fare breakdown shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 08:19:14, payment_status CHARGED, with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 and refund_if_voided_sgd of 5.00 under POL-NS-24. The rider filed this dispute, so a ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is FULL_REFUND of the whole contested 5.00 SGD under POL-GEN-03, with no driver compensation.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this is about the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged at 08:19:14 on 22 Aug 2026 for trip TRP-05057. The rider filed and asks that fee back.

Two things are not in dispute and I accept them. The driver did make the contact POL-NS-23 requires: the chat log (EV-CHAT-05057) carries his message at 08:07:10 and the trip record (EV-TRIP-05057) carries his in-app call at 08:15:20, both before the 08:19:10 cancellation, so the fee is not voided on the contact limb. And the amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-05057) shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and its own check reports the amount matches policy, so the POL-NS-22 referral for a mis-stated amount is not engaged.

The case turns on where the driver actually was. The trip record's arrival event is a button the driver pressed at 08:06:50, and under this policy an arrival tap records only that the driver set it. The policy's arrival test corroborates that event against the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05057) within 50 m for a STANDARD pickup. It is not corroborated: the nearest fix in the 120 s window around the arrival, at 08:04:50, is 476.59 m from the Block 251 pickup and reports an accuracy of 8 m — inside the 25 m filter, so it is a real reading, not a bad fix — and from 08:06:50 to 08:18:50 the vehicle is stationary roughly 650 m from the pickup. The driver's own messages agree: at 08:07:10 he says 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark', while the booking record's pickup label and the rider's 08:11:30 message ('I'm at Blk 251 drop off, where are you?') place the meeting point at Block 251. So the driver waited, but at the wrong block. His trace is complete (47 fixes at 30 s, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s), so the arrival test is not impaired and I take its result. The driver's answer — that the record's own deadline check returns arrived_by_deadline true — fails because that check is computed from the arrival button alone, and the button is the very thing the arrival test exists to verify; once corroboration fails, the tap establishes nothing about this trip.

POL-NS-24 therefore applies: it asks whether the driver arrived at the pickup location by the scheduled pickup time (08:10:00) plus 5 minutes (08:15:00), and on the corroborated trace he never did. The driver's POL-NS-21 point — that the 300 s free wait ran from 08:10:00 and expired before the 08:19:10 cancellation — is right about the clock but not about the substance: a free wait is a wait at the pickup, and a vehicle parked ~650 m away at another block has not satisfied it. The driver's point that the trace shows a stationary vehicle proves only that he stopped somewhere, not that he stopped where the rider was.

POL-GEN-03 therefore gives FULL_REFUND: amount_sgd 5.00 (the whole contested amount), driver_compensation_sgd null — the money goes back to the rider, nothing moves to the driver.

On referrals: POL-NS-24's second limb (the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit) is not triggered, because the driver did attempt contact by message and call, so no referral arises under it. POL-NS-25 does not fire — the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d count, and the fee does not stand, so the condition cannot be met. POL-NS-22's amount referral does not fire because the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD. No traffic advisory was attached (EV-ADVIS-05057-01 is absent, weight 0.0, and carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3)), but no no-show clause needs a traffic record, so its absence leaves no fact the policy requires unestablished and POL-GEN-26 is not engaged.

Confidence 0.90: every artifact carrying the deciding fact (the GPS trace, the trip record and the chat log) has full weight 1.0, and the contested amount (5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, with no fraud flag on either side) leaves the AI ruling final under POL-NS-26.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this dispute is about the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider at 08:19:14 on trip TRP-05057. The rider says the driver waited at the wrong block; the driver says he waited more than 10 minutes at the pickup and the rider never came. The record decides it for the rider.

The no-show policy's arrival test requires the trip record's arrival event to be corroborated by the GPS trace within the arrival radius, which is 50 m for a STANDARD pickup zone (POL-NS-21). It is not corroborated. The driver's own device trace (EV-GPS-05057) puts the vehicle no closer than 476.59 m from Block 251 anywhere in the 120-second window around the marked 08:06:50 arrival, and the vehicle then sits stationary roughly 650 m away from 08:06:50 through 08:18:50. The nearest fix reports an 8 m horizontal accuracy, well inside the 25 m accuracy filter, so this is not a bad reading. The driver's own chat message at 08:07:10 reads 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark', while the booking label and the rider's 08:11:30 message put the meeting point at Block 251 (EV-CHAT-05057). The driver's later message, 'I'm at the pickup point waiting already', is a bare assertion his own trace contradicts. The driver was never at the pickup.

Because the driver never reached the pickup location, he failed to arrive by the scheduled 08:10:00 plus 5 minutes, i.e. by 08:15:00. Under POL-NS-24 the rider may cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full. The 5.00 SGD charged at 08:19:14 must therefore be returned to the rider: FULL_REFUND of the whole contested 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation.

On the driver's surviving points: I accept that the POL-NS-23 contact obligation is met (a driver message at 08:07:10 and an in-app call at 08:15:20, both before the 08:19:10 cancellation), but POL-NS-23 is not the fee's foundation and does not save it. POL-NS-22 would transfer the fee to the driver only 'where the fee stands'; it does not stand here, so the claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION at 5.00 SGD is rejected, as is the argument that the record's own arrived_by_deadline check settles the matter: that check is computed from the driver's arrival tap, and a tap a party sets records only that he set it, whereas the arrival test requires the tap to be corroborated by the trace. The free-wait timers (expiry 08:15:00, cancellation 08:19:10) are taken as correct but are outweighed, because they presuppose a driver waiting at the pickup, and the driver was not there. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05057-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and is needed by no rule, so no POL-GEN-26 escalation arises.

No referral fires. The fee charged, 5.00 SGD, matches the policy fee, so POL-NS-22's mis-stated-amount referral is not engaged; POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit requires that the driver also failed to attempt contact, and he did attempt it; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag counts only where the fee stands, which it does not.

The confidence is capped by the deciding fact's carriers, all at weight 1.0 (the GPS trace, the chat log and the trip record). The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final.

The 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged at 08:19:14 is refunded to you in full. Both parties agree, and I find, that the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was met — he sent an in-app message at 08:07:10 and placed an in-app call at 08:15:20, both before the 08:19:10 cancellation — so POL-NS-23 is not a refund ground. The refund rests on POL-NS-24 instead: the driver never arrived at the pickup location.

The policy's own arrival test (POL-NS-21) asks whether the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within 50 m for a STANDARD pickup. The marked arrival is 08:06:50, but the nearest fix inside the 120 s window is index 18 at 08:04:50, 476.59 m away, and it reports an accuracy of 8.0 m — inside the 25 m filter, so this is not the product of a bad fix. From 08:06:50 to 08:18:50 every fix is stationary at roughly 650 m from Block 251, Hougang Avenue 3. An arrival tap is a status the driver sets; it records only that he pressed it, and the trace does not support it. On POL-NS-24 the driver failed to arrive at the pickup location by the scheduled pickup time (08:10) plus 5 minutes (08:15), and the fee charged is therefore refunded in full — 5.00 SGD.

The driver's points do not save the fee. The free-wait arithmetic (wait runs from scheduled_at 08:10, expires 08:15:00, cancellation 08:19:10) is correct, but a free wait is a wait at the pickup, and the arrival it presupposes is not made out; the record's arrived_by_deadline check reads that same uncorroborated button press. The stationary trace (25 fixes at speed 0) shows the vehicle standing still — standing still about 650 m from the pickup, not at it.
